instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Apologize Properly
cards.instruction: Get someone to deliver the apology in the form, order, and setting you consider valid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I rubbed my hands like you. Apology begun. Now say you're sorry for eating my cake at that table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was warming them. I'm sorry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hands ready. It's a promising rehearsal; the cake plate is over there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your dad's sitting there. Can't we do this privately?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He watched me blame the dog. Tell him you ate it before you tell me you're sorry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my name in red like yours. Apology heading. Your email needs to mention the broken vase.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I marked a spelling error. It says 'sorry.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Spelling first. For all I know, you're sorry about the font. Put the vase in the subject.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send 'Sorry about the vase' to Mum. She still thinks you broke it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with 'I broke it.' My name comes out before your apology goes in.

cards.title: Get It on the Record
cards.instruction: Get formal approval, endorsement, or acknowledgment before anyone can quietly revise their position.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I ticked the budget like you. Approved, then. Initial it before lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ticked where the sums need checking. I said yes in principle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Arithmetic noted. You said yes to the fireworks last year too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And I changed my mind when the costs doubled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then date your yes in principle. Put 'subject to checking the sums' beside it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've circled the fence post like you. Boundary agreed. Sign that the fence can stay before I pay the builder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I marked the rotten post. I suppose the fence can stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Posts marked. Put 'can stay' beside your name before I pay for new ones.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want to promise forever.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Date it today, then. If you change your mind, we'll know which permission changed.

cards.title: Assigned by Procedure
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept an unwanted responsibility by proving that the rules, rotation, or tradition make it theirs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've drawn a box round your Tuesday like yours. Rotation settled. It's your bin night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That box is next month's holiday. I did your Thursday last week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Away marked. And I did your Tuesday. The swap box says 'one week only.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You added that swap box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At your request, so I couldn't keep your easy Tuesday. You're due it back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've slid my keys across like you. Presidential handover. Congratulations; those are the toilet keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was returning a spare. I thought the caretaker cleaned the toilets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Spare accounted for. We voted to save that fee; the minutes assign closing and cleaning to the president.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I proposed that when you were president.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, and I cleaned them all year. Your first duty is continuing your savings.

cards.title: Complete the Record
cards.instruction: Get someone to fill the missing gaps in an account without revealing which answer matters most to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three taps, like you. Log opened. What were the mileage, fuel level and person at the wheel after nine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was counting change. You mean who dented the car?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Change checked. I mean all three blanks. Start with mileage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who was driving I remember. The rest means going down six flights to the glovebox.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fetch the book and bring you tea on the way back. Then give me the whole row in order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've circled all three headings like you. Now, arrival, departure and kitchen time, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was circling stains. Are you asking about the missing cake?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Marks in place. The cake can have its own line. What time did you arrive?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was late. Your cake was already cut by then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put 'late' until you can check. Now departure; that blank needs an answer too.

cards.title: Make It Official
cards.instruction: Recruit someone by giving them a title, role, or ceremonial duty that makes participation feel binding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I nodded to match you. Appointment accepted. You're Keeper of the Festival Lantern.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was greeting Jo. I only said I'd hold it while you tied your shoe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Jo witnessed it, then. An excellent probationary performance; here's your badge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How long is the appointment?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Until you find a qualified successor. The lantern must never be abandoned.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I clapped with you. Patron welcomed. Will you open our roof appeal and thank the donors?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was killing a moth. I can come, but I won't make a speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hall checked. Accept the patron's ribbon and lead the applause instead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I leave after the first donation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The patron applauds every donor. We couldn't have the later ones thinking their money mattered less.
